sessions.artist: Saracen repeat FRS session - first TX 15 January 1982 recorded 1981-12-09 for Friday Rock Show

sessions.details: Originally recorded on 9 May 1977 and broadcast on the John Peel Show.

track_listing.track: 'Gangland' (LP - The Number Of The Beast) EMI
'Shapes Of Things' (10" LP - The Single Hits) Charly
'You Give Me All I Need' (LP - Blackout) Harvest
'Tearin' Out My Heart' (LP - Straight Between The Eyes) Polydor

transcript.text: On 275 and 285. Also in stereo on VHF. This is National Radio 1.
David, keep taking the old black coffee.
Hello there, this is TV on the Radio here, Thomas the Vance. And welcome once again to The Friday Rock Show.
Okay, in The Friday Rock Show tonight we feature out of the archives guitarist John McLaughlin along with the Indian group Shakti, recording way back in 1977.
Plus we have a repeat of our recent session by the ace band called Saracen.
New releases by Uriah Heep, Motorhead, Crossfire, Asia, Rainbow, and the band called Tank.
Some classics by Neil Young and the Yardbirds, plus some you'll find in the Friday Night Connection.
We've also got the answer to the Friday Night Connection we set a fortnight ago.
But this evening, we start with this.
Trapped from the new Uriah Heep lineup, well, some of them are new and some of them are not,
[Music]
the album is called Abominog, and it's just come out.
It was called Running All Night, and Uriah Heep are now Lee Kerslake, Peter Golby,
John Sinclair, Bob Daisley and Mick Box.
Good album.
Before that, you heard of Iron Maiden,
a track from their album which has gone straight in this week
at the number one position in our country.
The track that we played was called Gangland.
The Uriah Heap track was for Andrew Marriott,
who lives up there in Crook in County Durham,
and both tracks were especially for all the heavies
at the Glenmore Estate, Hilden in Lisbon,
especially Radley and Crookie and Tony,
Leslie, Mandy and Irene, Bisbee, Cavazee
and all the ones in Hill Street.
And also for a load of people who are currently en route for Paris.
They should be en route. They were supposed to leave at nine o'clock from an academy up there in Lanarkshire in Scotland.
And those people include Alan Pearce and Charles Murray.
And also I've got to say hello to Alan Steele and most especially to all the teachers who organised the trip, especially Miss Cornwall.
Have a good time in Gay Parry. This is Neil Young.
That was Saracen. It's a repeat of our session by them that was just recorded before Christmas.
[Music]
[Music]
Good track called Crusader, which you'll also find a version of on their current album, which is entitled Heroes, Saints and Fools.
I'm proud of that Neil Young and a classic track called Southern Man,
and that was most especially for a gentleman who sent me what he calls a kinky postcard.
I think that's kinky, I think it's nice.
And he wanted me to say hello to Liz from York from She Knows Who,
the man from the Golden Void in Bedford.
Also, Southern Man was most especially for a fellow by the name of Mark,
who's got a birthday today.
Happy birthday, Mark, from a special lady called Sally.
Quick mention for Chris, who's also got a birthday today from Rosie, his wife.
The Gill family live in Litchfield in Staffordshire.
A little letter here from Alice Lee Park in Coventry.
Wants me to mention a load of people, so I shall.
Gaz and Charlie and Jason and Paul and Pete and Clive and Warren.
Steva and Porter, that should be Peter, not Porter, that's Irish for beer.
Martin and Sharon and Jane and Jane Barrett and Denise and another Jane and Collett and Martin and Paul Taylor.
And Andy McCausland, all in Coventry.
It's exactly 10.30. This is the Friday Rock Show from BBC Radio 1.
Way back in 1977, we recorded this.
John McLaughlin and the Indian group called Shakti, with two numbers.
And that was recorded on Monday the 9th of May, way back in 1977.
[Music]
The British guitarist John McLaughlin and the Indian group called Shakti.
Two tracks there, one was called Kriti, that was the last track,
and the track you heard before that was entitled Two Sisters.
We've got a ten-minute piece by him, but that won't be following till,
oh, something like ten, eleven-thirty, rather, tonight.
Now, here's Motorhead.
Track that came out way back in 1966 as a single by the Yardbirds.
It was called Shapes of Things.
As far as I can work it out, Jeff Beck was the guy who played the lead guitar on that.
It's from a 10-inch album that came out quite recently on the Charlie record label,
which is called The Yardbirds, The Single Hits.
And it really is an ace compilation.
It's got all their really good stuff on it.
Before that, something from the latest album by Motorhead.
It was called Speed Freak.
And I played that because Stephen Pillsworth, I think it is, of Sauceton in Cambridge,
sent me the sorry saga of the Motorhead tank raven super tent gig
that will not now be happening on Easter Monday.
Send me all the press clippings and it's a shame.
I'd also like to say hello, as I am trying to use my voice at the moment,
to everybody at the Milburn Academy fourth year.
They've all just had their exams, it seems,
particularly David has got 93%,
Keith and RTP and Rob the Haircut and Fishy and Brush Scopey,
and last and least, it says here, Prune.
And Brian Felsend.
Last but least. Talk about cheeky.
Have a listen to this. This was recorded live in the studio with very, very few overdubs.
The actual sound isn't really that great, but the playing is excellent.
They're a Belgian band called Crossfire.
That's from our session by Saracen.
It's called Flame of Youth, and before that, something by Crossfire,
from a compilation album that was sent to us from Holland.
It's on the Ray Vaughan record label, but the band are called, as I said, Crossfire.
They are from Belgium. I think they're really good players.
The track you heard was called Real Steel.
7 minutes now to 11, the Friday Rock Show from BBC Radio 1.
Hello to Graham from a fellow by the name of Nev in Droitwich.
Kat gets a mention from Sal and Div,
a couple of ladies who are in Salisbury Road, Braymore,
near Fording Bridge in Hance.
And finally, I found this little letter here,
which actually should have gone along with the Motorhead track.
It's from Ian Percival, who just says at the bottom of the letter,
I think Motorhead and ACDC are the greatest things ever to walk the earth.
Thank you, Spider. Here's Asia.
The guitar sound like that, that just had to be, of course, Steve Howe.
Indeed it was.
John Whetton was on the lead vocals, he plays the bass.
Carl Palmer rather plays the drums and Jeff Downs is on the old keyboards.
They're called Asia.
The album is doing so much better in America than it is here,
but I note this week it has gone into our album charts at roundabout number 24.
A lot of people I spoke to said it was quite wimpish when they first heard it,
but I think it really does grow on you.
Great musicians, Asia, and here comes the feeling.
Right, it's time for the Friday Night Connection.
Now, four nights ago we played you these three tracks
And we got one correct answer out of the bag.
There were more than one.
There was more than one correct answer, but we only have one, of course.
The correct answer that we've chosen has come from N.J. Hollis of 108 Bromley Heath Road.
I think it's Dormand in Bristol.
Mr. Hollis, you don't give me your first name, but I'll just call you N.
N.J. Hi, N.J.
You get yourself a £10 record token, of course.
The tracks we played a fortnight ago were these.
White Car from Drama by Yes.
Red Barchetta from Moving Pictures by Rush
and Terminus Eldorado from Scream Dream by Nugent.
Eldorado, Barchetta, white car.
Answer, cars.
Quite a lot of people got it right in actual fact,
but it's MJ who gets, as I said, the £10 record token.
He also put together one, two, three, four, five, six choices of connections,
but we've chosen this one.
Three bits of music with a connection or theme contained therein.
Start listening now.
Let me take you far away, you'd like a day.
Let me take you far away, you'd like a holiday.
To the cold days, for the sun, a good time.
Let me take you far away, and you'd tell a dream.
And that's our Friday Night Connection for tonight.
Put together by N.J. Ellis of 108 Bromley Heath Road down there in Bristol.
Wrote on his letter, got one at last, Tom.
And he certainly did. You just heard it.
Do you know what it is?
If you think you do, jot it down on a postcard
or any form of communication that you care to employ,
excluding the telephone.
And send your answer to The Friday Night Connection,
The Friday Rock Show, BBC Radio 1, London, W1A4WW.
And if you win, you get yourself a £10 record token
and also a T-shirt as well.
Now, I'm just going to have to guess at the size of NJ Ellis
because he hasn't indicated whether he's small, medium or large.
But NJ will be sending you an Asia T-shirt.
It's actually a sweatshirt.
It really is a nice piece of sweatshirt.
Whatever your size is, you're going to get a medium T-shirt from Asia.
And congratulations on getting it right.
Once again, the address is The Friday Night Connection,
The Friday Rock Show, BBC Radio 1, London, W1A4WW.
And good luck.
1124, this is something from the Scorpions' new album, Ban.
And that's from our repeat session by Saracen.
The track was called Jekyll and Hyde.
And before that, something from Blackout, the new album by the Scorpions.
It was called You Give Me All I Need.
Scorpion's track was for Kevin, Ian and Marcus and Mike and Neil.
And especially for me, me being Dave Corbin of Pool in Dorset.
Dave is going to miss the Scorpions on their current tour, he says,
because he's got a school study trip.
It's a shame, Dave, because they're an excellent band.
Nick Davidson sent me a little letter here.
He's in Godalming in Surrey.
Would I say hello to Adrian in Devices?
in Wiltshire. Of course I would. From Nick.
And also hi to Anna Gillette, I think
it is, in Basham, Chichester.
Or maybe Barsham. Or maybe Bosham.
Also, could I mention the band
called Witness. Nick is a member of the band called
Witness. Hello, Witness.
Malcolm Kuhn of Penzance in Cornwall
gets a mention. From The
Smiler, also in Cornwall.
And Richard Peck
of Northamberside wants me to say hello
to loads of people. Tony and
Tracy Shores and Chalky Booth and Drooper
Dave Holmes. And also the
Railway Arthur, it says here,
Chris Harrison, not the rugby player, Steve Hunt,
and me best mate Keith Allen
and his better half by the name of Hilda.
And thanks for letting me know that I came,
what is it, number one in the psychedelic chart
with a thing I recorded umpteen million years ago
called Summertime and the Living is Easy.
I sing that so out of tune, it's an absolute joke.
Or is it?
This is John McLaughlin and Shakti.
Well, I think the playing on that is absolutely stunning.
It was recorded in 1977.
John McLaughlin on lead guitar, he's British.
Al Shankar on violin.
Zakir Hussain on tabla.
T.H. Vinayakram on gatham, I think it's pronounced.
and Nancy and Poonah on what I believe are called struti boxes,
and they are the devices that make that droning sound
that sort of envelops the whole thing.
It's like the drones, I suppose, on the pipes, isn't it?
The track was called La Danse de Bonheur.
It's exactly 16 minutes to midnight.
A quick reminder that Radio 1 is going to be on the air all night tonight
with a marathon music quiz.
That'll be from midnight until 7 o'clock in the morning.
I'm afraid you're going to have to guess at the title of this track
because I haven't got what's known as a track listing for this particular record.
I've only got what's known as a white label.
There are no details on it whatsoever.
I don't know what this is called, though I do know who the band are.
This is from the forthcoming album by Rainbow.
That is by Tank.
It's from their album, which is out at the moment.
The track was called He Fell In Love With A Storm Pool.
